The '''2021–22 La Liga''', also known as '''La Liga Santander''' due to sponsorship reasons, was the 91st season of [[La Liga]], Spain's premier football competition. It began on 13 August 2021 and concluded on 22 May 2022.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-division/2021/06/16/60c9ce4946163f8d548b467d.html| title= Hay acuerdo: la Liga 2021-22 empieza el fin de semana del 13-15 de agosto|publisher = Marca |language=es | date= 16 June 2021| access-date= 17 June 2021}}</ref> The fixtures were announced on 30 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cdn1.sefutbol.com/pdf/calendario_1d_2122.pdf |title=Primera División Calendario |publisher=SEFutbol |language=es |date=30 June 2021 |access-date=30 June 2021 |archive-date=2 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210702075311/https://cdn1.sefutbol.com/pdf/calendario_1d_2122.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 24 June 2021, the Spanish [[Council of Ministers (Spain)|Council of Ministers]] resolved that spectators could return to stadiums at full capacity by means of a modification of the royal decree regulating the 'new normality', in the context of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/laliga/20210624/410214800104/el-publico-volvera-a-los-estadios-con-total-normalidad-la-proxima-temporada.html|title= El Publico volvera a los escenarios con total normalidad la proxima temporada| website= Mundo Deportivo| date= 24 June 2021| access-date= 24 June 2021 }}</ref>

[[Atlético Madrid]] were the defending champions, having won their eleventh title the previous season. [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] and [[Rayo Vallecano]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2020–21 Segunda División]]. They replaced [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] and [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], which were relegated to Segunda the [[2020–21 La Liga|previous season]].

[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] secured a record-extending 35th title with four matches to spare on 30 April, following a 4–0 victory over Espanyol.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/real-madrid-proclaimed-champions-of-laliga-santander-2021-22|title=Real Madrid proclaimed champions of LaLiga Santander 2021/22|publisher=La Liga|date=30 April 2022|access-date=30 April 2022|archive-date=4 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220604074500/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/real-madrid-proclaimed-champions-of-laliga-santander-2021-22|url-status=dead}}</ref>

This was the first La Liga season since [[2003–04 La Liga|2003–04]] that did not feature the league's [[List of La Liga top scorers|all-time top goal scorer]] [[Lionel Messi]] and long time [[Real Madrid]] player and captain [[Sergio Ramos]], who both departed for [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the summer.

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of twenty teams contested the league, including seventeen sides from the [[2020–21 La Liga|2020–21 season]] and three promoted from the [[2020–21 Segunda División]]. This included the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2021 Segunda División play-offs|promotion play-offs]].

;Teams relegated to Segunda División

The first team to be relegated from [[La Liga]] were [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], after a 1–4 loss to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 16 May 2021, ending their seven-year stay in the top tier.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eibar Relegated from La Liga With Loss at Valencia, Alaves and Getafe Secure Their Top-Flight Spots|url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/liga/2020-2021/eibar-relegated-from-la-liga-with-loss-at-valencia-alaves-and-getafe-secure-their-top-flight-spots_sto8323057/story.shtml|publisher=Eurosport|access-date=16 May 2020}}</ref> The second team to be relegated were [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]], following a 1–2 home defeat against [[Atlético Madrid]] on 22 May 2021, in their final game of the season, ending their three-year stay in the top tier. The third and final team to be relegated were [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], after drawing 0–0 against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 22 May 2021 in their final game of the season, suffering an immediate return to the second division.

;Teams promoted from Segunda División

On 8 May 2021, [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] became the first side to mathematically be promoted, assured of a return to the top flight following a 0–0 draw against [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RCD Espanyol are on their way back up to LaLiga Santander|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-ES/news/rcd-espanyol-are-on-their-way-back-up-to-laliga-santander|publisher=La Liga|date=8 May 2021|access-date=25 December 2021|archive-date=20 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210620114007/https://www.laliga.com/en-ES/news/rcd-espanyol-are-on-their-way-back-up-to-laliga-santander|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-08 |title=We will have a Catalan derby! Espanyol promoted to the First Division |url=https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/laliga/will-have-derbi-catalan-the-espanyol-rises-to-the-first-division_268245_102.html |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=FCBN |language=en}}</ref> The second team to earn promotion was [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], following [[UD Almería|Almería's]] 2–3 loss to [[FC Cartagena|Cartagena]] on 18 May 2021. Both teams made an immediate return to the first division after a season away.<ref>{{Cite web |publisher=Reuters |date=2021-05-18 |title=Mallorca promoted back to LaLiga |url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/05/18/soccer/1621373625_946865.html |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=Diario AS |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-18 |title=Mallorca join Espanyol in La Liga promotion |url=https://global.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37617394/real-mallorca-join-segunda-winners-espanyol-la-liga-promotion |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Benevento relegated from Serie A as Real Mallorca promoted to La Liga - European round-up |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12310464/benevento-relegated-from-serie-a-as-real-mallorca-promoted-to-la-liga-european-round-up |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> The third and final team to be promoted were [[Rayo Vallecano]], after winning the play-off final 3–2 against [[Girona FC|Girona]] on 20 June 2021, returning after a two-year absence.

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy|Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest goals-to-games ratio. A goalkeeper had to have played at least 28 games of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/primera-division/zamora.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|work=MARCA.com|date=4 September 2017 }}</ref>

==Attendance to stadiums==
===Restrictions===
Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, clubs were not allowed to use the total capacity of their stadiums. According to the progress of the pandemic, the capacity allowed each month was decided by the Government of Spain, in agreement with the Autonomous Communities.

*August (rounds 1 to 3): 40% of capacity allowed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/espana/2021-08-04/sanidad-vuelta-estadios-abonados-aforo_3216783/|publisher=El Confidencial|language=es|date=4 August 2021|title=Luz verde a la vuelta a los estadios: un 40% de aforo, pero las CCAA podrán reducirlo}}</ref> Additionally, the Basque Country reduced it to 20%,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ondacero.es/emisoras/pais-vasco/noticias/gobierno-vasco-marca-20-aforo-estadios-que-situacion-epidemiologica-mejore_20210806610d0fe75e57db0001e0812d.html|publisher=Onda Cero|language=es|date=6 August 2021|title=El Gobierno Vasco marca un 20% de aforo en los estadios hasta que la situación epidemiológica mejore}}</ref> Catalonia to 30%<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/catalunya/noticia-catalunya-fija-aforo-30-grandes-eventos-deportivos-exteriores-20210809162644.html|publisher=Europa Press|language=es|date=9 August 2021|title=Catalunya fija un aforo del 30% para los grandes eventos deportivos exteriores}}</ref> and the Valencian Community limited the attendance to a maximum of 15,000 spectators, always respecting the agreement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/espana/comunidad-valenciana/abci-generalitat-valenciana-modifica-restricciones-para-permitir-15000-espectadores-estadios-202108061216_noticia.html|publisher=ABC|date=7 August 2021|title=La Generalitat Valenciana modifica las restricciones para permitir 15.000 espectadores en los estadios}}</ref>
*September (rounds 4 to 7): 60% of capacity allowed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/diarioas/2021/09/01/actualidad/1630495398_228041.html|publisher=Diario As|language=es|date=1 September 2021|title=Sanidad y las comunidades elevan los aforos en los estadios: porcentajes en LaLiga y ACB}}</ref> The Basque Country raised its own limit to 30%,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2021/08/30/primera/1630323463_048919.html|language=es|title=El Gobierno Vasco amplía el aforo de los estadios al 30%|date=30 August 2021}}</ref> while Catalonia did to 40%.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/espana/cataluna/2021-09-07/cataluna-reuniones-restricciones-covid_3276454/|publisher=El Confidencial|language=es|date=7 September 2021|title=El Govern aumenta a un 40% el aforo en estadios al aire libre y mantiene el cierre del ocio nocturno}}</ref>
*October (rounds 8 to 12): full capacity allowed, except for Catalonia and Basque Country, whose governments limited the attendance to 60%.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/2021/09/29/61540694e2704e2a0c8b4581.html|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=29 September 2021|language=es|title=Vuelve el público al 100% a los estadios de LaLiga y al 80% en la ACB}}</ref>
